text.p: Schnitzer Steel Industries Inc on Thursday reported second quarter earnings that it said "disappointed" the company, but it said it expects improvement in its earnings throughout the rest of fiscal 1997 and in fiscal 1998.

President Robert Philip said in a statement that expected improvements in selling prices for scrap metal should "result in increasingly larger contributions to our earnings over the next several quarters."

Earlier Schnitzer, a large scrap metal recycler in the western United States, reported second quarter earnings of $0.13 a share on sales of $76.6 million versus $0.65 a share on $82.7 million in sales one year ago.
Sales of ferrous scrap fell to $44.4 million in the second quarter from $59.3 million last year due to lower shipments and lower average selling prices.
In the third quarter, however, order prices are $13 per ton higher than the average price in the third quarter.
"We expect this to positively impact our ferrous scrap margins next quarter, Philip said.
Revenues in the company's steel operations rose 15 percent from fiscal 1996's second quarter to $35.6 million and shipments rose 17 percent to 105,200 tons.

"We expect to realize positive results from (our) new rod block, which is now operational and will expand our product line beginning in the third quarter of fiscal 1997. We should see increased tonnage and improved margins," Philip said.
Finally, the company said its strong cash flow, liquidity and balance sheet allow it to continue pursuing other scrap acquisitions.
